## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vanavacchattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, designated as Tha Ap 551 [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the biographical and karmic background of the elder (thera) Vanavaccha. The text is cataloged with five modern translations in five languages on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 108 shared passages across 28 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest degree of overlap occurs with commentaries and other Apadāna poems, particularly the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (17 matches), the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Cūḷasugandhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 552), and the *Kaṅkhārevatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 544), largely consisting of standardized formulaic verses (notably around segments §19–23) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with the Sanskrit *Divyāvadāna* (scoring up to 70) and lower-scoring parallels with the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) and *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
